h: The Midrash: the soul that sees and guards

p: — "Bless the LORD, O my soul," etc.
— that he blessed the Holy One, blessed be He, with the soul?
— Because the soul sees and is not seen, etc.;
, — the soul guards the body, etc.
— it counts five "Bless, O my soul"
— as said corresponding to the soul,
— the five levels within the soul

paragraphs.text: Genesis 24:1 — "And Abraham was old, coming into days, and the LORD blessed Abraham in everything." The verse opens the Tanchuma's homily and closes the maamar: the whole os is a reading of zaken (acquired wisdom) and ba ba-yamim (entry into the supernal days).

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Chayei Sarah 3 — "'And Abraham was old': this is what Scripture says, 'Bless the LORD, O my soul.' Why did David see fit to bless the Holy One, blessed be He, with the soul? Because the soul sees and is not seen … the soul guards the body, and the Holy One, blessed be He, guards the entire world." The same section ends: "'You are clothed in glory and majesty': of Your glory and Your majesty You clothed the head of Abraham, in that You gave him the splendor of old age." Rav Tzadok treats the Tanchuma's two comparisons as a short form of the Gemara's five. (The printing's abbreviation for "the Holy One, blessed be He," misprinted with a colon, is read as the abbreviation.)

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10a — "These five 'Bless the LORD, O my soul': with reference to whom did David say them? He said them only with reference to the Holy One, blessed be He, and with reference to the soul. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, fills the whole world, so the soul fills the whole body; … sees and is not seen …; … nourishes the whole world, so the soul nourishes the whole body; … is pure, so the soul is pure; … dwells in the innermost chambers, so the soul dwells in the innermost chambers." Rav Tzadok reads the five clauses in order as the stages of a person's life: from conception (fills and guards), to first sight in Torah, to thirteen (nourishes), to purity, to the innermost chambers (zaken). Editorial corrections made from this Gemara: the printing's "that the soul zakhah (the whole) body" (twice) is corrected to zanah (the Gemara's "nourishes", which is the third clause and the one his explanation needs); the masculine nir'eh ("is seen") → the feminine nir'eis; the truncated "yosh" → yoshev ("dwells").

h: Filling and guarding the body from conception

p: — "so too the neshamah fills the whole body,"
— Just as it lists regarding God, blessed be He,
— that He fills the whole world,
— "and the Holy One, blessed be He, guards the entire world"
— from when the body is formed,
— even though it has no understanding at all
— for the soul is given to a person
— and it guards the whole body.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 91b — "From when is the soul given to a person, from the time of conception or from the time of formation? … Rather, from the time of conception", Antoninus and Rabbi. Rav Tzadok uses it to set the first stage, the soul that fills and guards the body, before any understanding. The printing's "nesinah" (the same letters transposed) is corrected to the Gemara's nitnah ("is given").

h: Purity: the evil inclination returns, and is slaughtered only in the future

p: — just as at the time of the Giving of the Torah
— for the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts,
, — the evil inclination returned to its place,
— so too, even after he merits
— that the soul nourishes the body,
— so that he draws life from words of Torah,
— for the power of the evil inclination is nullified.
— the evil inclination has not been cleared away
— as it will be in the future,
— when the Holy One, blessed be He, will slaughter

h: The innermost chambers: the Yud enclosed by the closed Mem

p: "מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים
— "Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells in the innermost chambers,
— so too the neshamah dwells in the innermost chambers."
— alludes to the Yud of Chochmah,
— which is joined with the tip of the Yud
— This is the utterance "Let there be light,"
— together with the light that was hidden away.
— is enclosed by a closed Mem,
— showing that it will never again go out,
— (along the lines of what is written
בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק ג רלו עַמּוּד ב
— "the closed Mem is the supernal King"

paragraphs.text: Genesis 1:3; Chagigah 12a — "And God said, Let there be light"; and Chagigah 12a: the light of the first day, by which Adam saw from one end of the world to the other, was hidden away for the righteous in the future ("the light that was created on the first day … He hid it away for the righteous"). He uses it to explain the "chamber of Yud": the utterance of Chochmah together with the hidden light of Keser. (Address from the standard text; not opened in this session.)

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 236b (Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas) — "Why is it not closed? Because the closed Mem is the supernal King; the open Mem, the lower King." He reads chadarim as cheder Y-M (Yud, Mem): the Yud of Chochmah closed inside the final Mem of Binah, so that it "will never go out again." The printing's run-together abbreviation is read al derech mah she- ("in the manner of what is said"), and its "she-al yetze" as shelo yetze ("that it will not go out").
